note: Adjudicated variants: 7 accidental — five of punctuation, one of accent, and one of this edition's i/j orthography. Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

No comma before the apposition Fílium tuum, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w064 and ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018. The typical edition prints the comma; the corpus keeps its own rule, and the reading is recorded here so the choice is visible.

No comma after pétimus, with handmissal-eo, which prints the sentence unbroken: in do the comma marks the inserted rubric (osculatur Altare), which this edition carries as its own segment, and the same comma stands in the typical edition for the same reason.
No comma before the et joining the second subjunctive, with do and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.lavabo w061: hábeas and benedícas are one petition.
No comma before the et closing the series of four infinitives, with do and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.orate-fratres w021.
No comma before the et joining the bishop to the Pope, with do. In handmissal-eo the comma follows the name slot, which this edition does not print.

Accented, with do: fídei has three syllables and carries its stress mark (ORTHOGRAPHY.md). The hand missal prints it accented at Meménto étiam, so the omission here is an inconsistency of that one line.
